day-1.t: Day 1 — Pick a service buyers already search for

b.v: Today's goal

v: List three services you can do this week without learning anything new
Check that buyers actually search for them on Fiverr
Choose one and name it in the buyer's own words

b.v: About 20 minutes. Use a laptop or a browser on your phone. Keep a notebook open.

Most new sellers are not beaten by competition. They are beaten by choosing a service nobody is looking for. On Fiverr the buyer comes to you already knowing what they want to buy, so your first job is to stand where the buyers are standing.
1) Start from what you can show today
Write down every skill for which you could produce one sample file, sheet, picture or document before tonight. Not skills you plan to learn — skills you have.

v: Can I do this today, with the tools I already own?
Could I show one example, even one I made for a friend for free?
Would a stranger pay Rs 3,000 for it?

b.v: 2) Check demand before you write a single word
Fiverr is a search engine. If your service returns almost no results or every result looks abandoned, buyers are not there. Read how sellers write their titles and copy the wording, never the text.

Search like a buyer:|Open Fiverr and type your service in the search bar, for example excel data entry|Count the gigs on the first page and look at how many reviews the top three have|Note the exact words used in the titles around you|Write the number of results in your notebook
Do not pick a service because it looks easy. Easy services have the most sellers and the lowest prices. Pick the place where your skill meets a real search.
3) Narrow it until you are the obvious choice
A wide service puts you against thousands of sellers. A narrow one puts you in front of one type of buyer who feels understood.

v: wide = data entry (thousands of sellers)
narrow = PDF to Excel data entry for clinic and shop records
wide = logo design (huge competition)
narrow = simple logo and menu design for small Karachi food shops

b.v: Practice

Write three services in your notebook. Beside each one, write the number of gigs you found and one narrow version of it. Pick the narrow version that you can create a sample for tonight, and write that as your one-line promise, like this: I turn scanned shop records into clean Excel sheets, delivered in 24 hours.

day-2.t: Day 2 — A gig title and image that get the click

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write a title with the buyer's words, not yours
Make a simple gig image on your phone
Fill the search tags and category correctly

b.v: About 25 minutes. You need one free design app such as Canva, or any app you already know.

The title and the picture are the only two things a buyer sees in a list of twenty gigs. They decide in about two seconds whether to read the rest. A perfect description after a weak title is wasted work.
1) The title formula
Use this order: what you deliver + for whom + the format or tool. Keep it under about 80 characters so it is not cut off on a phone.

v: I will convert PDF bank statements into a clean Excel sheet
I will edit 10 short Urdu videos for TikTok in 24 hours
I will design a simple logo and menu for your cafe

b.v: 2) The image carries more weight than the words
Buyers scroll pictures, not text. Your image needs one clear subject, large readable text of five words or fewer, and your main promise in numbers if you have one.

Make the image:|Open a free design app and choose a square template, 1000 by 1000 pixels|Put your main promise in the biggest text, for example PDF TO EXCEL IN 24 HOURS|Add one small picture of the real work — a before and after screenshot|Change the background so it is not the default template colour everyone uses|Export as JPG or PNG and check that the text is readable at thumbnail size
Do not put your phone number, email address, WhatsApp number or website on the gig image. Contact details outside Fiverr are against the rules and can cost you the account.
3) Category and search tags

The category tells Fiverr where to show you. The tags are the search words attached to your gig. Choose the closest category, then pick tags as the phrases a buyer would type, not as the words you like.

@Title and tags worksheet
Deliverable: PDF to Excel conversion
For whom: small shops and clinics
Format: .xlsx file
Title: I will convert your PDF records into a clean Excel sheet
Tags: pdf to excel, data entry, excel formatting, convert pdf
Practice
Write one title using the formula and make one square image with no contact details. Save both in a folder named fiverr so you can reuse them when you change the gig later.
Today's goal

v: Decide what goes in Basic, Standard and Premium
Write package names a buyer understands
Put limits on revisions so the order stays profitable

b.v: About 20 minutes. Have Day 1's one-line promise in front of you.

Three packages are not three prices for the same work. They are three different sizes of work. When the sizes are clear, most buyers choose the middle one, and the cheap package stops eating your evening.
1) Design the sizes, not the discounts
Write the smallest useful job in Basic. Add one real extra in Standard. Premium should be work you would be happy to do for a full day.

v: Basic = one page or one file, one revision, 3 days
Standard = up to five pages, two revisions, 2 days
Premium = up to twenty pages, formatting and a summary sheet, 1 day

b.v: 2) Name the packages by the result
Basic, Standard and Premium are fine, but a short custom name tells the buyer what they get. Keep names to two or three words.

Write your three package rows:|Row 1 — name, pages or quantity, revisions, delivery days|Row 2 — same four things, larger|Row 3 — same four things, largest|Check that no package promises unlimited revisions|Check that Premium is still work you can finish in the stated days

Unlimited revisions is the fastest way to lose money on Fiverr. One buyer can then send changes for weeks. Write a number, and write what counts as a revision: a change to the delivered work, not new work added.
3) Say what is not included
The line that protects you is the exclusion line. Write it in the package description, not only in the main description.

@Package description
Basic — Up to 5 pages converted to Excel, 1 revision, delivered in 3 days.
Not included: new data added after delivery, formatting of charts, printing.
Need more pages? Choose Standard.
Practice
Write your three packages on one page with four columns: name, quantity, revisions, delivery days. Then add one sentence under each row that starts with Not included.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Set a price ladder you can climb

b.v: Today's goal

v: Choose a starting price that wins the first orders without sounding cheap
Plan the three price rises and what earns each one
Add extras that raise the order value

b.v: About 20 minutes. Check the current Fiverr fee before you set a price, because the percentage Fiverr keeps changes over time.
Your price is a message before it is money. Too high with zero reviews and nobody clicks. Too low and buyers assume the work is bad, and you attract the buyers who complain most.
1) Price for the first five reviews, not for profit
Your first orders are buying you proof, not income. Set a price slightly below the good sellers around you — not the cheapest on the page — and deliver more than the package says.

v: Look at the three cheapest gigs with real reviews, and the three best-reviewed gigs
Sit above the cheapest group, not inside it
Write down the exact price you will charge for the first five orders

b.v: 2) Raise the price on a rule, not on a mood
Decide now when the price goes up, so you are not guessing later. A simple ladder is one step for every five good reviews.

v: After 5 reviews: raise Basic by about 30 percent
After 10 reviews: raise all three packages and keep the same delivery days
After 20 reviews: remove the cheapest package if it still brings the worst buyers

b.v: Do not keep the same low price for a year because you are afraid. Buyers read a very low price as a warning, and you will be busy with the worst clients and none of the good ones.
3) Extras are where the money hides
Gig extras are paid add-ons a buyer ticks at checkout. They cost you little time and raise the average order without changing your main price.

v: Extra fast delivery in 24 hours
Extra source file or editable version
Extra page or extra item beyond the package
Extra short call to explain the work

b.v: Practice
Write your ladder on paper: today's price, the price after 5 reviews, after 10 and after 20. Then write three extras with a price for each. Keep the paper — you will use it in Day 10.

day-5.t: Day 5 — A description that answers objections

b.v: Today's goal

v: Write the first two lines that a buyer actually reads
Answer the five questions buyers ask before ordering
Close with one clear instruction

b.v: About 25 minutes. Write in short sentences. Assume the buyer is reading on a phone in a hurry.
A buyer does not read your description looking for reasons to hire you. They read looking for a reason to leave. Your job is to remove every doubt, in the order the doubts appear.
1) The first two lines decide everything
Only the first two lines show before the buyer taps more. Say what you deliver and for whom, in plain words. No greetings, no life story.

v: weak = Hello sir, I am a hardworking freelancer with 5 years experience and I love my work
strong = I convert scanned shop and clinic records into a clean Excel sheet with totals checked twice, delivered in 24 hours

b.v: 2) Answer the five objections
Write one short paragraph for each. If you cannot answer one, that is a gap in your offer, not in your writing.

v: Can you do my kind of file? — name two real examples
How long will it take? — give the days and say when the clock starts
What if it is wrong? — state your revision policy in one line
Why you and not the cheaper seller? — name one check you do that others skip
How do we start? — tell them to send the file and the message you need

b.v:
@Description skeleton
I convert scanned shop and clinic records into a clean Excel sheet, delivered in 24 hours.

WHAT YOU GET
- One .xlsx file, one row per record
- Totals checked twice before delivery
- Column names in English or Urdu, your choice

HOW IT WORKS
1. You send the file or photos and tell me the columns you need.
2. I confirm the price and the delivery day.
3. You get the sheet, and one round of corrections if anything is wrong.

WHAT I NEED FROM YOU
Clear photos or a readable PDF, and the column list.

Message me with your file and I will reply with a fixed price today.
Do not copy another seller's description and change two words. Fiverr removes copied gigs, and buyers recognise the text from three other gigs on the same page.
3) Keep it scannable
Use capital headings, short lines and dashes. A wall of one long paragraph is skipped, even when the content is good.
Practice
Write your description using the skeleton above with your own service. Then read only the first two lines out loud. If they do not say what you deliver and when, rewrite them.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Deliver on time and handle revisions

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build a five-minute pre-delivery check
Send a delivery message that reduces complaints
Handle a revision request without losing money or temper

b.v: About 20 minutes. Do this the first time you have a real order, or practise on a sample file.
Late delivery and unclear delivery cause more bad reviews than bad work. Buyers cannot see your effort. They see the clock and the file. So make both easy to trust.
1) Never deliver straight from your working file
The file you worked in has odd column widths, a stray note, and a name like final-final-2. Clean it, rename it, then deliver.

Pre-delivery check:|Open the file fresh and look at it as the buyer will|Check every total against the source, by hand, once|Delete test rows, hidden sheets and your own notes|Rename it clearly, for example shop-records-2026-03.xlsx|Write the delivery message before you attach anything
2) The delivery message
Three short parts: what is attached, what you checked, what happens next. This message is also your evidence if the buyer later says something was missing.

@Delivery message
Assalam o alaikum. Your file is attached: shop-records-2026-03.xlsx.

What is inside: 412 rows, one per sale, with columns Date, Item, Qty, Rate, Total.
Checks I did: row count matched the source, and the daily totals add up to the monthly total.

If any row needs a different column name, tell me within the revision round and I will fix it the same day.
Do not deliver and then go silent for a day. Delivery day is when buyers get nervous and look for problems. Stay near the chat for a few hours after you deliver.
3) Revisions: agree the scope, then do it fast
A revision is a correction of what was ordered. New work is a new order. Say this kindly and immediately — not after three free rounds.

v: If it is a correction: fix it the same day, no argument
If it is new work: thank them, give a price and a delivery day
If it is unclear: ask one question with two options, so they can answer in one word

b.v: Practice
Write your own delivery message template and save it in a notes app. Then take any file on your phone and run the five-minute check on it as if you were about to deliver it.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Reply fast and reply well

b.v: Today's goal

v: Set up notifications so you never miss a message for hours
Use three saved replies for the three questions you get most
Turn a first message into an order

b.v: About 15 minutes. Keep your phone charged and the Fiverr app installed.
Fiverr shows buyers how quickly a seller replies. A slow seller looks like a seller who will also be slow with the work. Most first orders go to whoever answers first with a clear next step.
1) First message: answer, then ask, then price
A buyer's first message is usually one line: can you do this? Reply with a short yes, one question that proves you read it, and a price or a reason you need to see the file.

@First reply
Yes, I can do this. Two things so I do not guess:
1. Is the PDF scanned or typed text?
2. How many pages?

For up to 10 pages the price is already on the gig. Send the file and I will confirm the delivery day today.
2) Three saved replies cover most of your day
Write them once, store them in your phone notes, paste and edit. Do not paste without editing the name and the detail — buyers can tell.

v: Price question: Yes, that is covered by the Standard package. If you need X as well, it is an extra and I can add it today.
Waiting for a file: I am ready to start. Send the file here and I will begin within the hour.
Revision received: Understood. I will send the corrected file today before 6 pm.

b.v: Do not reply with only the word price or send your rate card and nothing else. A number without a question reads like a shop, not a person, and buyers go quiet.
3) Protect your response time
Turn on app notifications for messages only, and set one hour in the morning and one at night when you clear the inbox. That is enough to stay fast without living in the app.

Set up now:|Install the Fiverr app and allow message notifications|Turn off notifications for everything else in the app|Choose two fixed times a day to check messages|Write your three saved replies in your notes app
Practice

Write your three saved replies today, with your own service words. Then send one real message to a seller you admire, asking one polite question about how they deliver — it teaches you how a good reply feels.

day-8.t: Day 8 — Ranking factors in plain words

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand what Fiverr rewards, without chasing tricks
Improve the two things you control most: clicks and completion
Stop copying advice that risks your account

b.v: About 20 minutes. No tool needed, just read and take notes.

Fiverr does not publish a formula. But every marketplace ranks on the same four ideas: does this listing match the search, do people click it, do they leave happy, and does the seller behave reliably. You can work on all four.
1) Match: does your gig answer the search
Put the buyer's search phrase in the title, the tags and the first lines of the description. Not repeated ten times — once, clearly, in the places the system reads.

v: Title: the exact phrase near the start
Tags: phrases buyers type, not single words
First two description lines: the same phrase again, naturally
Category: the closest one, even if another looks bigger

b.v: 2) Clicks: does the picture earn the tap
If your gig appears in search but nobody clicks, nothing else matters. Test a new image every few weeks and keep the one that brings more messages.

v: One subject, not four
Five words or fewer in large text
A real screenshot of the work, not a stock photo of a laptop
Colours that stand out from the row of white and blue around you

b.v: Never buy reviews, exchange reviews with another seller, or run several accounts to order from each other. This is the most common reason new accounts are closed permanently, and the money you paid is not returned.
3) Behaviour: reliability is a ranking signal
On-time delivery, quick replies, few cancellations and complete orders all feed your standing. One cancellation hurts more than one late night helps.

Weekly ranking check:|Search your main keyword and find your gig in the first three pages|Write down the position and the date|Read your last five buyer messages and note the repeated question|Fix one thing on the gig — image, title or package limits — and note the change
Practice
Search your keyword, find your gig, and write down its position plus the date. Then write one sentence describing what you will change this week and why.

day-9.t: Day 9 — Buyer requests, messages and staying unbanned

b.v: Today's goal

v: Reply to buyer requests in a way that gets read
Know the four actions that get accounts closed
Keep every conversation inside Fiverr

b.v: About 20 minutes. Read the rules page on Fiverr before you send anything today.

One closed account can end a year of work, and appeals usually fail. The rules are not complicated, but they are enforced by machines that read your messages, so a careless line can cost you everything.
1) Buyer requests: short, specific, priced
A buyer request is a posted job. Many sellers reply with a paragraph about themselves. The buyer reads the first line of each and skips the rest.

v: Line 1: the one detail in their post that shows you read it
Line 2: what you will deliver and when
Line 3: your price and one question

b.v:
@Buyer request reply
You need 600 product photos renamed by SKU before Friday.
I can do that: 600 files renamed in the exact pattern you showed, delivered Thursday night, with a list of any missing SKUs.
Price is on my gig for 500, plus a small extra for the last 100. Should the missing ones be renamed or left out?
2) Four things that get accounts closed
These are the ones beginners trip over. None of them are worth the risk.

v: Taking payment outside Fiverr, in any form, including a bank transfer, JazzCash or Easypaisa
Asking for or offering a good review in exchange for money, a discount or free work
Sharing your phone number, email, WhatsApp, Instagram or website in the chat or the image
Opening a second account after a warning, or ordering from yourself

b.v: If a buyer asks to pay you directly to save the fee, refuse politely and keep the order on Fiverr. That message is a trap as often as it is an honest request, and the account that gets closed is yours.
3) How to refuse without losing the buyer
You do not need to explain the rules. Offer the same value inside the platform and move on.

v: I have to keep everything inside Fiverr, it protects us both. I can send the file right here, and you can pay through the order.
I cannot take the work off the platform, but I can start today if you place the order now.

b.v: Practice
Write your refusal line in your notes app in your own words. Then read Fiverr's terms page and write down the two rules you were closest to breaking.

day-10.t: Day 10 — From zero to ten reviews

b.v: Today's goal

v: Get the first three orders without breaking any rule
Ask for a review in a way that is allowed and effective
Turn ten reviews into a steady flow of orders

b.v: About 25 minutes. Bring the price ladder you wrote on Day 4.
The first ten reviews are the hardest and the most valuable thing you will ever earn on Fiverr. After that, the reviews bring the buyers, and the buyers bring the reviews.
1) The first three orders come from small, specific gigs
New gigs with no reviews do not win big orders. They win small, clear, low-risk orders from buyers who need exactly that one thing. Make the smallest package genuinely useful and cheap enough to try.

v: Create one narrow gig for one clear job instead of one wide gig for everything
Keep the first package small: one file, one page, one fix
Reply within minutes during your chosen hours
Deliver a little more than the package promised, every time

b.v: 2) Asking for a review the right way
You may ask for an honest review. You may not ask for a good one, and you may not pay for it. Ask once, after delivery, when the buyer is happy — never before the work is done.

@Review request, after delivery
Thank you for the order. If the sheet is exactly what you needed, a short honest review helps other small shops find me. If something is not right, tell me first and I will fix it.
Do not message a buyer three times asking for a review, and never offer a discount for a five-star rating. Buyers report it, and Fiverr treats a bought review as fraud even when the work was real.
3) Turn ten reviews into a system
At ten reviews you have proof. Now use it in the places buyers look: the title stays the same, the image gets a line such as 40 orders delivered, and the description opens with your strongest result.

v: Add one line of proof to the gig image
Raise your prices to the ladder step you wrote on Day 4
Ask two happy buyers whether they need the same work monthly
Save every delivery message — they become your templates for the next year

b.v: Practice
Write your review request message now and save it. Then list three small, specific gigs you could publish this week, each for a job you can finish in under two hours.
